documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology and oncology practice. Consultation 01/01/2024 (holiday clinic session).
Reason: iron deficiency anemia with celiac disease, not responding to oral iron.

She tells us she still feels drained, gets winded with exertion and lightheaded if she stands up fast. Appetite has been poor. Celiac disease confirmed by biopsy in July; gluten-free since. Long history of heavy periods.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro with meals, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily (taking it regularly), ibuprofen 400 mg as needed. No known drug allergies.
Family: father type 1 diabetes, mother autoimmune thyroiditis, maternal aunt celiac.
Social: never smoker, alcohol rarely, preschool teacher.

Exam: pallor of skin and conjunctivae. Spoon-shaped nails on several fingers.

Labs today: Hgb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, RDW 18%. Iron 30 mcg/dL, TIBC 600 mcg/dL, transferrin saturation 5%.

Assessment: iron deficiency anemia from duodenal malabsorption and menstrual loss, with a full year of oral iron unable to keep up.
Plan: IV ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg, two doses one week apart, at our infusion center. Continue oral ferrous sulfate for now. CBC and ferritin in 6 to 8 weeks. Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Infusion Center Record
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Infusion center treatment summary.
01/08/2024: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV over 15 minutes. Vitals stable before and after. No reaction. Observed 30 minutes.
01/16/2024: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV, second and final dose of this course. Tolerated without reaction.
Total 1,500 mg. Labs to be drawn in about 6 weeks.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group, seen 01/16/2024.
Type 1 diabetes; celiac disease on a gluten-free diet since July 2023; iron deficiency anemia, IV iron through hematology this month. A1c 7.1%, interpret with caution given recent anemia. Post-meal readings steadier since going gluten-free; two mild lows a week before lunch, lispro breakfast dose trimmed.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, ibuprofen as needed. NKDA.
Urine microalbumin normal. Next visit June.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to say the iron infusions are working, I have actual energy at the end of the school day for the first time in a year. Hematology wants labs in March. Should I keep the iron pills too?

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So glad to hear it! Yes, keep the pills going unless hematology tells you otherwise, they help top off stores with your periods. I'll watch for the March labs.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology. Follow-up 03/05/2024.
Good response to IV iron: Hgb 12.3, ferritin 96. Energy much better, no dizziness. Continue ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily and gluten-free diet. Given ongoing heavy menses and celiac, we suggest CBC and ferritin every 6 months through your office; please refer back if Hgb falls below 11 or ferritin below 15.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30F annual.

Feeling like herself again after the January infusions. Gluten-free 9 months; mostly strict at home, harder at school events and eating out, admits a few slips. Bowels mostly normal. Weight up 3 kg since fall. Periods still heavy. Endo visit coming in June.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro per scale, ferrous sulfate daily, ibuprofen prn. NKDA. Never smoker.

Exam: color much better. Thyroid normal. RRR, no murmur today. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nondistended. Skin clear. Feet normal.

A/P
1. IDA - responded to IV iron (Hgb 12.3, ferritin 96 in March). Continue oral iron; CBC/ferritin every 6 months per hematology.
2. Celiac - doing well; reviewed that even small exposures matter.
3. T1DM - endo. Urine microalbumin, CMP, lipids today.
4. HM: PCV20 today given diabetes. Pap 2026. Flu/COVID in fall.
RTC fall for labs and visit.

documents.title: Endocrinology Visit Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Seen 06/27/2024 for her scheduled diabetes visit.

She raised two new problems: aching bones, mostly in the legs, and frequent muscle cramps over the spring. She also reports that the diarrhea and bloating have crept back, especially after bread and pasta; she thinks she has been getting gluten at school functions and from shared kitchen items. Family history is notable for autoimmune disease.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro by scale, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, ibuprofen as needed. NKDA.

Exam: pale. Abdomen slightly distended, soft. Tenderness over the shins and thighs on palpation; proximal leg strength mildly reduced.

Labs 06/27: calcium 8.1 mg/dL, phosphorus 2.5 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 120 U/L, intact PTH 95 pg/mL, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 12 ng/mL. tTG IgA 38 U/mL (down from 142 at diagnosis but not normal). A1c 7.0%.

Assessment:
1. Vitamin D deficiency with a raised PTH, from celiac malabsorption, explaining the bone pain and cramps.
2. Celiac disease with ongoing gluten exposure by history and serology.
3. Type 1 diabetes, at target.

Plan: ergocalciferol 50,000 units weekly for 8 weeks, calcium carbonate 500 mg twice daily with food (separate from iron). Recheck calcium, PTH and vitamin D in 3 months. Recommend a return visit with her dietitian. Diabetes regimen unchanged.

documents.title: Pill timing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Endo started me on vitamin D once a week and calcium twice a day. They said keep the calcium away from the iron. Is it ok if I do iron in the morning and calcium with lunch and dinner?

documents.title: RE: Pill timing
documents.author: RN
documents.body: That schedule works well. Iron first thing, calcium with lunch and dinner, vitamin D any day of the week with a meal. I've added them to your med list.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule (2,000 units) by mouth daily
medications.reason: Vitamin D deficiency, maintenance; prescribed by endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology Lab Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, result letter for labs 09/24/2024.
25-hydroxyvitamin D 31 ng/mL, PTH 58 pg/mL, calcium 9.0 mg/dL. Repletion complete; cramps and bone aches much improved per phone check-in. Ergocalciferol finished; start cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily as maintenance and continue calcium carbonate 500 mg twice daily. Repeat vitamin D at her next visit.

orders.reason: recurrent iron deficiency anemia, Hgb 10.4, ferritin 10

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 30F with celiac, T1DM, IDA. Due for the 6-month CBC that hematology asked for, and she is tired again, slowly since about July, more out of breath carrying kids' bins upstairs. Vitamin D course done per endo, cramps gone. Since the endo visit she has gone back over her dietitian handouts and tightened up the diet. Periods unchanged, heavy. Taking ferrous sulfate most days. Eats very little red meat, never has liked it.
Meds: glargine, lispro, ferrous sulfate, cholecalciferol 2000 u daily, calcium carbonate 500 bid, ibuprofen prn. NKDA.

O: mild pallor. RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Hgb 10.4, ferritin 10 today.

A/P
1. Recurrent iron deficiency anemia - stores depleted again 9 months after IV iron. Back to hematology per their threshold. Continue oral iron.
2. Celiac - recent gluten exposure likely played a part; better adherence now.
3. Vitamin D deficiency - repleted, on maintenance per endo.
4. Flu and COVID given today.
Hematology referral placed.
